description: NExtSEEK Knowledge Graph — lightweight schema for parser routing decisions

node_types.label: Sample
node_types.description: A biological sample, schema 1.2. Property 'type' holds the sample type code (e.g. TIS, CEL, DNA, D.SEQ, NHP, MUS) and the node also carries a type label, T_ plus its code (T_TIS, T_D_SEQ). 'uuid' holds the sample identifier (the UID), whose grammar is <TYPE>-<YYMMDD><LAB>-<n>: the three letters after the date are the lab's code, so a lab or PI scope is a match on the UID. Every non-empty metadata attribute of a sample is a property on its node, named exactly as the attribute title: descriptive fields (Scientist, Notes, Name, Organ, Sex, storage, treatment, concentration, shipping, imaging, etc.), Protocol, and the lineage family Parent, AntibodyParent, BacteriaParent, CompensationFCSParent, ParentF, ParentM and Treatment1Parent..Treatment5Parent. Numeric and date attributes are stored typed, so they compare with < and >. 'search_text' holds every value of the sample, UID included, for text found anywhere in the record, and 'project_ids' its projects. Every key containing 'Parent' names an ancestor. Samples link to each other via DERIVED_FROM, to studies via IN_STUDY and to projects via IN_PROJECT.

node_types.label: SampleType / Attribute
node_types.description: The catalog: one SampleType per sample type code and, through HAS_ATTRIBUTE, one Attribute per attribute title that type carries, with how many samples fill it and its value type. It answers which types carry a field, which fields a type has, and how a key is spelled across types.

node_types.label: Study
node_types.description: A research study grouping samples. In this instance a study IS a published paper: 'title' is the paper title. The publication properties are 'DOI' and 'PMID' — UPPERCASE, unlike every other property on this node. A study is published when its DOI or PMID is a non-empty string. The unset value is an empty string, NOT null, so never test IS NOT NULL: it is true for every study. Use coalesce(st.DOI,'') <> '' instead. Most studies are unpublished, which is expected rather than missing data. Linked to an Investigation via IN_INVESTIGATION.

node_types.label: Investigation
node_types.description: A project grouping one or more studies. Property 'title'. Known values: BioMicroCenter, CSBC, Collagen Study, Endometriosis, GBM_BTC, Impactb Investigation, MIT_SRP, MetNet, and TCGA, which is not on every instance (loaded on local and dev only).

node_types.label: Project
node_types.description: A SEEK project. Property 'title'. Samples link to it via IN_PROJECT, investigations via IN_PROJECT.

relationships.note: Carries assay and protocol metadata on the relationship (internal_assay_title, protocol_title). Used to traverse from derived data back to source samples.
Links a sample directly to the study it belongs to.
Links a study to its parent investigation/project.
Links a sample (and an investigation) to its SEEK project.

graph_query_triggers: Query scopes to a named Study ('in the GBM_BTC study', 'in the MetNet study', 'what samples exist in study X')
Query scopes to a named Investigation or Project ('in the MetNet project', 'in the MIT_SRP investigation', 'what studies are in project X')
Query asks what studies, projects, or investigations contain or relate to something ('what projects have mouse samples', 'which investigations have NHP samples with sequencing')
Query counts or aggregates within a study or investigation scope ('how many samples are in the GBM_BTC study', 'how many TIS samples exist across all studies')

Query asks about assay or protocol application by vocabulary name ('processed via Tissue Collection', 'underwent Short Read Sequencing', 'associated with flow cytometry protocol', 'samples that underwent single cell sequencing') — especially when no clean REST endpoint exists for the combination
Query mixes Sample results with Study or Investigation membership in the same output

Query asks about ancestry, parentage or derivation by a lineage property rather than a UID ('samples whose AntibodyParent is set', 'what is the parent of X', 'trace the lineage of', 'samples with a Treatment1Parent') — the Parent-family properties live on the Sample node and only the graph can filter or traverse them
Query asks which samples have any parent of a given kind, or counts samples by lineage property ('how many samples have a BacteriaParent', 'which CEL samples have ParentF set')

Query asks which paper or publication a sample appears in ('what paper is this sample from', 'is UID X published', 'which publication used these samples') — traverse (s:Sample)-[:IN_STUDY]->(st:Study) and read st.DOI / st.PMID
Query names a paper by title, DOI, or PMID and asks for its samples ('what samples were used in the SureQuant paper', 'samples for 10.1101/2021.09.30.462577', 'samples in PMID 34981053')

Query finds, lists or counts samples by sample type, keyword or attribute value, with or without a study scope ('find tissue samples mentioning X', 'how many slides are stained with H&E', 'samples whose Vendor is X') — every metadata attribute is a property on the Sample node and 'search_text' holds every value
Query compares a number or a date ('greater than', 'at least', 'between', 'before 2021') — numeric and date attributes are stored typed on the graph
Query combines conditions that must all hold (two keywords, a keyword and a field, several fields) — Cypher ANDs them

Query asks for a count, a breakdown by type or by field, the distinct values of an attribute, or how a value or a key is spelled across records (spelling variants, duplicates, which records use a key)
Query scopes samples to a lab or PI ('the X lab') — the lab code sits inside the UID (ENTITY_RESULT.lab_codes); or names any other person as who made or handled samples — the Scientist attribute
Query asks for all samples in the database, or a count across every type
api_preferred_triggers: Catalog records themselves (assays, sample types, SOPs, projects, investigations as records) → the matching catalog endpoint
The full metadata record, an export or a download of samples named by UID → admin/samples/retrieve; an explicit request to see or visualise the lineage tree of one UID → sample-tree
PATCH/update on a specific sample UID
Any non-metadata intent that maps cleanly to a known API endpoint in the catalog
disambiguation_rules: If the query mentions a study or investigation by name → graph_query, even if a sampletype is also present
If the query says 'how many X in study Y' or 'across all studies' → graph_query
If the query says 'how many X' with no study/investigation scope and no time span → graph_query, a count of samples (not reporter)

If the query has entity-resolved sampletype + assay codes AND no study/investigation scope AND the assay is used as a keyword attribute filter (not a named assay/protocol traversal) → graph_query, matching the term as text on the samples of that type

If the query asks for samples 'associated with', 'that underwent', or 'processed via' a named assay or protocol → graph_query (assay metadata lives on DERIVED_FROM relationships, not on sample records; REST endpoints cannot filter on it)
If the query asks for parent samples that have children of multiple types → graph_query (lineage: the graph checks a descendant of every required type)
If the query involves project-level upload counts or statistics over time → reporter (not graph_query)

If the query filters or reports on a descriptive sample attribute (Scientist, Notes, Name, storage, treatment, concentration, dates, shipping, imaging fields) → graph_query. The attribute is a property of the Sample node; advanced_search matches text anywhere in a record and cannot restrict it to one attribute, compare numbers, AND two terms or aggregate.
If the query concerns lineage structure (parents, children, ancestry, derivation chains, any 'Parent' property) → graph_query, even when a specific UID is present.
Investigation titles to recognize (case-insensitive): BioMicroCenter, CSBC, Collagen Study, Endometriosis, GBM_BTC, Impactb Investigation, MIT_SRP, MetNet, TCGA (TCGA is not on every instance)
If the query mentions a DOI, a PMID, a paper, or a publication → graph_query (DOI/PMID live on Study nodes and no REST endpoint filters samples by them)

If the query is a plain keyword or attribute search with no scope at all ('find X samples', 'samples mentioning Y') → graph_query; REST sample searches serve only refinements of a result that came from REST

If the query names a person: a lab or PI (ENTITY_RESULT.labs / lab_codes) → graph_query on the lab code inside UIDs; anyone else → graph_query on the Scientist attribute. Never /people/, which lists registered user accounts
